examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Interrupts transfer control to a handler; vectors identify handler entry through a supplied code/table. Polling repeatedly tests status and can consume CPU work. DMA moves blocks with limited CPU involvement but can contend for the memory bus. Daisy-chain position supplies hardware priority. Total transfer time may include setup, arbitration and completion overhead, so raw data rate alone is not always sufficient.

**Key relationship:** DMA setup and completion use CPU time; individual data transfers are controller-driven

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify polling, interrupt or DMA roles.
2. Separate CPU overhead from transfer time.
3. Apply priority and bus-sharing assumptions.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For polling cost, multiply checks per second by time per check and add actual-event processing. Interrupt cost multiplies events per second by per-event service time. DMA transfers in bytes per stolen cycle must be converted to bits per second if requested. Vectored handlers identify an entry quickly; daisy-chain priority is not CPU polling of all devices.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A 10 MHz CPU gives DMA 2% of its cycles, transferring 4 bytes per stolen cycle. Find throughput in bits/s.

**Answer: 6400000.** DMA receives 0.02·10⁷=200000 cycles/s. Each cycle transfers 4·8=32 bits. Rate=200000·32=6400000 bits/s. The percentage is applied to cycles, not to the size of a transfer.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An interrupt normally changes execution mode and runs a handler; it does not necessarily cause a different process to be scheduled.

DMA does not mean the CPU has no involvement at all.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

DMA primarily reduces CPU work by:

- **A.** Transferring blocks without CPU copying every word
- **B.** Removing all setup costs
- **C.** Replacing the instruction set
- **D.** Eliminating memory

**Answer: A.** The CPU configures the operation, while the DMA engine moves the data and reports completion.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** DMA may contend for the memory bus
- **B.** Vectored interrupts help identify handler entry
- **C.** Polling can consume repeated CPU checks
- **D.** DMA always needs zero CPU instructions

**Answer: A, B, C.** Setup and completion usually require CPU participation, making the absolute claim in D false.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

A DMA block contains 4096 bytes and transfers 512 bytes per burst. Number of bursts?



**Answer: 8.** 4096/512=8 full bursts; no partial burst is needed.

#### Pattern 4 · NAT · Transfer problem

DMA transfers 64 KiB over a bus moving two bytes per 100 ns cycle. Ignoring setup and contention, transfer time in milliseconds?



**Answer: 3.2768.** 64 KiB=65536 bytes. Required cycles=65536/2=32768. Time=32768·100 ns=3276800 ns=3.2768 ms. Keep byte/word and ns/ms conversions separate.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q34 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/interrupts-dma?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** I/O interfaces, interrupts and DMA. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Polling every 10 ms makes 100 polls per second. At 100 μs each, this consumes 10,000 μs=10 ms. Processing the one keystroke adds 0.2 ms.
2. Thus T1=0.0102 seconds per second. Interrupt handling consumes 1 ms per keystroke, so T2=0.001.
3. Their ratio is 0.0102/0.001=**10.2**.

#### GATE 2024 CS1 · Q15 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/interrupts-dma?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** I/O interfaces, interrupts and DMA. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Cycle stealing transfers a word in a stolen bus cycle, and burst DMA amortizes bus acquisition over a block: A and B are true.
2. Programmed I/O occupies the CPU polling or moving data, whereas interrupt-driven I/O lets it do other work while waiting. The asserted better CPU utilization in C is false.
3. Vectored interrupts directly identify the handler, supporting D. The requested false statement is **C**.
